text:
The abstract outlines a comprehensive review that emphasizes the importance of optimizing nanofluid characteristics (type, size, concentration, base fluid, dispersants) and their delivery via advanced MQL systems (nozzle design, atomization, controllable supply) to improve machining performance across turning, milling, and grinding. It highlights the need to understand the underlying tribological and heat‑transfer mechanisms at the tool‑workpiece interface, linking nanofluid parameters to machining outcomes. This directly aligns with the candidate hypothesis, which posits that tailored nanofluid properties and optimized MQL delivery—combined with mechanistic insight—significantly enhance machining performance. Therefore, the study’s evidence supports the candidate as its main hypothesis.
